title: Shakira Says 'No Way!' to Fake Campaign Pics
summary: Pop star Shakira is setting the record straight! Recently, pictures popped up online showing her with two people running for president in Colombia, her home country. The images made it look like she was cheering for them. But Shakira says, "Nope, not true!" She told everyone the pictures are fake. "I do not support any candidate," she said. "And nobody asked me if they could use my face." This isn't the first time people tried to connect her to one of the candidates, Iván Cepeda. Earlier, some folks spread a rumor that they were distant cousins—also not true. Shakira made it clear she's not telling anyone who to vote for. "My commitment is to Colombia and its democracy," she explained. "Every Colombian should choose freely. I just want the elections to be peaceful and fair." Shakira has spoken up about big issues before. Last year, she talked about how scary it can be to be an immigrant in America. She said we should always treat people with kindness, no matter what. Right now, Shakira is super busy with her world tour. She just played four sold-out shows in Colombia in February, and this weekend she's performing in Miami. So while some people are busy making up stories, Shakira is busy making music—and making sure the truth is heard!
why_it_matters: When you see a picture of a celebrity online, it might be fake, so learning to question what you see helps you not be tricked—a skill that matters for your whole life.

keywords.explanation: A candidate is a person trying to be chosen for a job, like president, in an election.
Democracy is a system where citizens choose their leaders by voting in free elections.
An immigrant is a person who moves from one country to live in another country.
A rumor is a story passed around that may not be true; people often spread rumors without checking facts.
Sold-out shows mean every seat at the concert was bought, so the venue was completely full.

background_read: Shakira (born in Barranquilla, Colombia, she is a Grammy-winning pop star known for hits like 'Hips Don't Lie') has always been proud of her home country. Iván Cepeda is a Colombian senator who is now running for president. During elections, fake images (sometimes made with computer tricks) can spread online and fool voters. Colombia has a history of political tensions, and false news can affect how people vote. By speaking out, Shakira reminds everyone to check facts before believing what they see.
Article_Structure: WHO: Shakira, a world-famous singer, and two Colombian presidential candidates (including Iván Cepeda).
WHAT: Fake pictures online made it look like Shakira supported candidates, but she publicly denied any endorsement.
WHERE: The images spread on the internet, especially in Colombia.
WHY: Shakira wanted to stop false information and ensure that voters know she is not telling anyone who to choose, protecting fair elections.

perspectives.description: Shakira believes in democracy and wants voters to decide freely without being swayed by lies using her image.
Using fake images to associate a celebrity with a candidate cheats voters and harms trust in elections.
This shows how easy it is to create and spread fake content today, raising the need for tools to detect manipulated photos.
